author: Mya Falgout
title: Supreme Court reviews execution case of Mobile man - NewsBreak
text:
By Mya Falgout ,
1 hours ago
MOBILE, Ala. ( WKRG ) — The Supreme Court is trying to decide whether a Mobile County man should be executed for a crime committed in 1997.
Mobile man arrested after police chase, allegedly hitting vehicles: MPD Joseph Clinton Smith, 55, has been on death row for almost half his life for beating a man to death in a truck with a hammer and stealing $150 from him almost 30 years ago.
Alabama is still trying to get the man charged with capital murder despite his being found “intellectually disabled” by lower courts a few years ago.
As of now, Smith is still protected by the Supreme Court since it stopped executions for those who fall under this disability in 2002 — something the high court is now being asked to reconsider.
Dawson Hicks is an Alabama anti-death penalty advocate who works directly with those on death row and says this potential decision is a violation of human rights.
“Obviously, this is an intellectually disabled man. This is someone who does not have the same facilities as, like, a fully mentally cognitive person. And one, the Supreme Court has already ruled that this is an abuse of human rights, that this is morally wrong to execute someone in his state,” said Dawson Hicks, with Project Hope to Abolish the Death Penalty in Alabama.
However, Smith’s IQ test scores are slightly too high. Alabama law defines intellectual disability as an IQ of 70. His five scores range from 72 to 78.
“We see this as just the latest attempt in a series of many of the state of Alabama and the entire now, at this point, federal government as a whole, trying to expand the use of executions and capital punishment,” Hicks said.
For Hicks he sees that there are other ways to hold these criminals accountable.
“We advocate for rehabilitation and more mercy-based approaches to criminal justice. And that’s not to say that harm doesn’t happen and that crimes don’t happen because they absolutely do. And innocent people are hurt or even have their lives taken as a result of that,” Hicks said.
Goo Goo Dolls to perform at The Wharf The Supreme Court is expected to make a decision on Smith’s case by June.
